openscriptures_strongs.label: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary via Open Scriptures
openscriptures_strongs.declared_from: The entry's own structure, read across all 23,646 routes on 14,929 definition records and 5,939 keys. This digitization keeps Strong's two fields apart, so a route's definition is either the KJV rendering list (7,503 records) or Strong's own sentence (7,426 records); the store takes the list whole (8,203 routes, 0 slices) and takes the sentence both whole (7,515) and in slices (7,928, from 4,738 records). The same mark reads differently in the two fields: in the list a depth-0 comma separates renderings; in the sentence it is mostly Strong's own punctuation. Every one of the 52,371 mark occurrences in route text falls in exactly one shape; 0 unexplained. The inventory's closed set (18 marks) agrees mark for mark, occurrences and routes; the definition text uses no mark outside it.

regions.locate: Field first: a definition carrying the x (U+00D7) or + sign is the KJV rendering list; else one that ends with '.' (or with '.' and one bracketed note) and carries no tag trace (a non-digit, a space, then , ; or .) is the KJV rendering list; else it is Strong's own definition sentence. Corroborated by the store itself: 0 of 7,503 list records carry a slice route; 4,738 of 7,426 sentence records do. In the list field the list ends at its full stop (period.list_end) and what follows is a note. In the sentence field a space before , ; or . is the trace of the provider's tagging of a definition word (the tag trace).

,.evidence: אדר: (become) glorious, honourable. | אדר: Adar , the 12th Hebrew month | דמע: a tear ; figuratively, juice
,.falsifier: A list piece cut at a depth-0 comma that is not a rendering on its own: 2 pieces led by a syllable and 16 pieces that are one group alone ('(perplexed)'), out of 18,795 pieces today (open question 7). precedence: field (Strong's sentence | the KJV rendering list)
. (period.list_end: the last rendering | the note after the list)
; (semicolon.rendering_separator in the list; semicolon.sense_separator in the sentence)
, (comma.rendering_separator in the list; comma.def_between_tagged_glosses in the sentence)
openscriptures_strongs.precedence_note: Scope before every cut: nothing inside ( ) or [ ] is cut. The field decides which comma shapes exist at all; the list's full stop decides that commas after it are a note's, not renderings'; ';' and ',' then cut at depth 0. In the sentence the comma test reads the piece bounded by the nearest depth-0 ';' or ',', so ';' is read first.

slice_cut_through_a_group.rule: a slice route is never divided; it ships as the store cut it

unbalanced_parentheses.conflict: Today's engine holds a damaged sense back (gloss-store drops it from the pool): 34 routes carry one; 21 of them divide under this declaration and the rest print whole.

hyphen_attachment.rule: ship whole: no syllable is attached

marks.where: list field, depth 0, before the full stop
sentence field, depth 0, the tag trace on both sides

separates_on.rule: Locate the field, then cut only at the shapes above, at depth 0 and before any unclosed '('. Every piece is kept and is a run of the provider's own characters; the cut character is the mark, not the reading (so the list's full stop is not printed as part of its last rendering). A note after the list is kept as a piece and marked as a note, never offered as a reading. No piece is joined to another, no group is distributed across its head, no syllable is attached, no × or + is stripped. A slice route is never divided.
separates_on.declared_from: 5,026 routes divide into 18,795 pieces (list 3,389, definition 1,637); 272 of the pieces are notes. The other 18,620 routes are one reading each. Pieces that fail to rejoin: 0.
separates_on.machine: declaration-v1.mjs applies separates_on.mark alone and has no field test, no list end and no tag trace; under it this object (no 'mark') ships every route whole. Applying it needs the locate step ledger.mjs codes (fieldOf, listEndOf, shapeOf, declared).

open_for_the_owner.q: The comma between two tagged glosses in Strong's sentence ('to expose , dismiss ,').
open_for_the_owner.reading_a: It divides (declared): 363 commas in 242 routes; the provider tagged both sides as definition words.
open_for_the_owner.reading_b: Each sense stays whole: the store already carries these glosses as slice routes on the same record (left gloss 205, right gloss 215 of 363), so dividing prints them a second time in their sentence form ('to expose' beside 'expose').

open_for_the_owner.q: The comma after a tagged gloss before the definition's last piece, where the right side's tag cannot be seen.
open_for_the_owner.reading_a: It divides like the one above: 490 commas in 490 routes; the right piece is itself a slice route in 164.
open_for_the_owner.reading_b: It stays whole (declared): the last piece is sometimes a qualifier ('to carve , whether wood or stone'), and the characters cannot tell which.

openscriptures_strongs.not_done_here: The definition is never mined for a reading: a route is read where the store cut it. The store's slice routes (cut from Strong's sentence) are not judged here; whether a slice is a separation or a derivation is the derivation section's question (declarations-v1.json, openscriptures_strongs pairs). No group is distributed, no syllable attached, no × or + stripped, no lone group re-joined, nothing withheld for damage.
